items.title: PathwayTheme: identifying and attributing pathway-level axes of variation in omics data
items.blurb: Exploring gene expression datasets often involves delineating principal axes of variation corresponding to either biological or technical variables. Principal component analysis (PCA) is typically employed as it uses all genes, reflecting global relationships between samples. Existing tools decompose gene expression first and interpret components afterwards. However, gene-level components are sensitive to sparsity and difficult to relate directly to biology, signals carried by low-variance components are easily overlooked, and differential pathway analysis is usually performed separately, on thresholded gene lists. PathwayTheme addresses these limitations by reversing the order of operations: per-sample pathway scores are generated first and then decomposed by PCA, so that each component is defined by pathways and can be tested directly against biological and technical variables. PathwayTheme further incorporates a statistical framework for supervised differential pathway enrichment that does not require thresholded gene lists, with Gene Ontology results summarised into themes. Applied to a published paediatric cancer cohort, PathwayTheme separated technical from biological axes and identified components distinguishing sample types, diagnoses and genetic subgroups, including rare groups represented by low-variance components.

items.title: Multi-omics causal deep learning reveals regulatory structure while interventions refine perturbation predictions
items.blurb: Inferring gene regulation from single-cell data is difficult because observational measurements cannot distinguish correlation from causation and access to perturbational data, especially with multiple modalities, remains limited. Here we present the Cross-Modal Causal Variational Autoencoder (CMC-VAE), which learns a network linking genes and proteins (gene-gene, protein-protein and gene-protein) in the latent space and maps each connection back onto measured features. Trained on 809,130 observational CITE-seq profiles, CMC-VAE recovers co-expression, transcription factor regulons and immune signalling programs, and learns a sparse cross-modal map enriched for transcript-protein cognate pairs. On three CRISPR screens used during development, it ranks knockout-responsive genes better than correlation and latent-VAE baselines. Fitted to a screen's unperturbed control cells, without perturbation labels, the model translates measured knockout RNA responses into protein responses better than a correlation map and cognate transcripts. The direction of gene-to-gene regulation, however, is not recovered from observational data. On the CITE-seq screens, fine-tuning only the latent network improves held-out response correlation, mainly by learning a response shared across knockouts. On larger Perturb-seq screens, with about 1,000 training perturbations, fine-tuning the latent network learns gene-specific effects that transfer to held-out genes, more so than a gene-level causal model fine-tuned on the same cells, and in simulation, such interventions also restore edge orientations that observational training leaves unresolved.

items.title: Disentangling within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
items.blurb: Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution characterization of gene expression and cellular organization in situ. Resolving within-cell-type heterogeneity is essential for understanding how cellular states relate to tissue function and disease. However, imperfect cell segmentation and RNA spillover can contaminate cell-level expression profiles, obscuring intrinsic expression patterns and generating spurious variation. Existing decontamination methods can struggle to distinguish intrinsic variation from contamination when both are inferred from spatial measurements alone, and may suppress genuine state-associated signals when within-cell-type heterogeneity is not explicitly modeled. Here we present Dancer, a reference-guided probabilistic framework that disentangles within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination by combining cell-type-specific gene programs learned from single-cell data with explicit modeling of intrinsic expression, neighboring-cell contamination and background RNA. Across multiple human tumor datasets with varying gene compositions and panel sizes, Dancer improves cell-type separation and expression specificity while preserving identity-associated signals, achieving superior overall performance in benchmark comparisons. Inferred gene program activities reveal within-cell-type heterogeneity in the form of distinct cellular states and continuous spatial gradients associated with local tissue environments, while reference-guided panel expansion extends molecular characterization beyond the measured genes. Together, Dancer supports accurate transcript decontamination and more faithful interpretation of cellular heterogeneity within its native tissue context.

items.title: To sort or to hash? Revisiting k-mer counting
items.blurb: Motivation: Counting k-mers in large genomic datasets is a foundational primitive in bioinformatics, supporting applications such as genome assembly, variant discovery, metagenomic profiling, and sequence database indexing. As sequencing throughput grows, k-mer counting is routinely applied to collections of hundreds to thousands of files. Even a modest per-file speedup compounds into hours of saved computation across such collections. Methods: Sorting and hashing are the two main ways of counting k-mers, and practice has largely settled on the former, of which KMC3 (Kokot et al., 2017) is the most refined expression. We reconsider this choice and analyze both approaches using a cost model that charges computation and memory transfers together. We show that the outcome of the comparison rests on two matters: how abundant the k-mers are, and whether the hash tables fit in cache. Sorting is faster only when data is mostly unique and the hash tables do not fit in cache. We then design a k-mer counting algorithm in the light of this analysis. We adopt the consolidated paradigm based on first partitioning the k-mers by their minimizer, thus obtaining partitions of super-k-mers, and then counting each partition independently in parallel. In particular, super-k-mers are deduplicated before counting, and the number of partitions is chosen so that the hash tables fit in cache whenever possible. The algorithm avoids writing temporary data to disk if enough internal memory is available. Results: We implemented this strategy in a tool named Tuna and show that it is faster than KMC3 on all but one of our inputs, spanning bacterial and human assemblies, metagenomes and read sets, by up to 4.3x. The advantage of Tuna compared to KMC3 in the counting step alone widens to 6.8x as k-mer abundance grows, as the analysis predicts. On the largest input tested, 614 GB of human sequencing reads, Tuna counts within 4 GB of memory and 0.7 TB of temporary disk. On that input the two tools finish within 1.1x of each other under the full 256 GB budget, and restricting every tool to the same 8 GB budget widens the advantage of Tuna over KMC3 to 1.8x. Software: The software is freely available at github.com/vicLeva/tuna under the MIT license.

items.title: Evaluating the Nanopore Inosine Model for ADAR-Dependent A-to-I RNA Editing Detection
items.blurb: Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) reads native RNA molecules, and its basecaller now includes models that detect RNA modifications directly, among them inosine, the product of adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing by ADAR enzymes. These models are increasingly used, but how reliably they detect modifications in biological samples has rarely been tested. We evaluated the Dorado inosine model in a mouse macrophage cell line, comparing wild-type cells with ADAR1-knockout cells and in vitro transcribed RNA, before and after an inflammatory stimulus that increases editing. As a reference, we used the editing sites identified by Illumina sequencing of the same cells. We assessed whether the model distinguishes edited from unedited RNA, which negative control is needed to identify editing sites, how many reference sites are recovered, and why sites are missed. The confidence of the Nanopore inosine model alone was not sufficient to identify editing, and a matched ADAR-deficient control was essential. Even with this control, detection was limited by sequencing depth, by low editing levels and by basecalling errors at edited positions. Nanopore sequencing can detect A-to-I editing, but its inosine calls require an ADAR-deficient control and sufficient depth, and should be confirmed by an orthogonal method.

items.title: Confidence-guided spatial gene expression inference for reliability-aware prognostic analysis from histology
items.blurb: Inferring spatial gene expression from histology images offers a promising strategy for extending spatial molecular profiling to large-scale clinical tissue archives. However, existing approaches face two major challenges: limited generalizability of single-cell expression inference across datasets and platforms, and the lack of reliable estimates of prediction uncertainty, which compromise downstream biological and clinical analyses. Here, we present REGAIN, a framework for spatial gene expression inference at both single-cell and spot resolutions with prediction confidence. Across tissue sections, independent datasets and platforms, REGAIN improved spatial gene expression prediction and downstream analysis. Confidence-guided selection further enriched for cells with more accurately recovered expression profiles and improved cell-type annotation, while confidence-weighted clustering enhanced spatial-domain identification. Beyond assessing prediction quality, confidence mapping reveals greater heterogeneity in gene expression predictability across spatial domains than across broad cell types, with differences persisting within the same cell type and associated with tumor progression-related cell states and local microenvironmental context. Importantly, in 766 patients from the TCGA-BRCA cohort, confidence weighting enhanced the prognostic value of histology-inferred spatial molecular features, yielding stronger prognostic associations and identifying additional prognostic information beyond age and PAM50 molecular subtype. These confidence-weighted features also showed improved prognostic discrimination compared with clinical variables alone or combined with unweighted spatial molecular features. Together, REGAIN marks a shift in histology-based spatial gene expression inference from a focus on predictive accuracy toward a reliability-aware paradigm, demonstrating that prediction confidence provides biological insights into morphology-expression coupling and enhances the clinical informativeness of inferred spatial molecular features.

items.title: Structural clustering of paired αβ T-cell receptor repertoires recovers antigen-specific convergence beyond sequence similarity
items.blurb: T-cell receptor (TCR) antigen recognition depends on the three-dimensional geometry of the paired {beta} complementarity-determining regions (CDRs), which primary sequence does not fully capture. Most repertoire-clustering methods group receptors by CDR3 motifs, sequence distance or V-J gene usage, and may miss receptors that differ in sequence but adopt similar loop conformations. We present SPACE-TCR (Structural Profiling of Alpha-Beta Clonotypes by Epitope), which stratifies predicted paired {beta} backbone models by CDR length, aligns them on conserved framework anchors and clusters them by C RMSD across the CDRs. On an independently curated benchmark of 4,779 paired CD8 TCRs spanning 367 epitopes, 94.6% of SPACE-TCR clusters at the focal 0.75 [A] threshold had purity [≥] 0.9, close to ClusTCR (97.3%), while clustering more than twice as many unique CDR3{beta} (10.4% versus 4.7%); every method that clustered more did so at markedly lower purity. SPACE-TCR had the lowest polyspecificity (5.4%), and 22.7% of its high-purity clusters were sequence-diverse or sequence-unrelated, categories rarely recovered by the evaluated CDR3{beta}-similarity methods. With increasing unannotated repertoire background, it kept higher purity than the evaluated sequence-based methods across all available comparisons (30.4% at 89.2% noise, compared with 15.0% for TCRMatch). Paired structural clustering therefore complements sequence-based analysis, recovering convergent receptor families that sequence criteria miss.

items.title: GlycanPUG: WURCS-Based Heterogeneous Graph Pretraining for Structurally Ambiguous Glycans
items.blurb: Background: Glycans orchestrate diverse biological processes, yet they remain underrepresented in computational biology compared to proteins and nucleic acids. Although WURCS 2.0 provides a machine-readable structural representation that preserves uncertainty, the evaluated IUPAC-based deterministic workflow processes 43.1% of the GlyCosmos-derived cohort examined here, motivating approaches that retain structural ambiguity. Methods: To overcome this limitation, GlycanPUG (Probabilistic Uncertainty-aware Graph) was introduced as a pretrained graph model for glycan representation learning. By leveraging WURCS 2.0, GlycanPUG represents candidate linkages and substituent attachments using weighted edges and uncertainty attributes within a heterogeneous graph framework. A 4-layer Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with a dedicated node pre-enhancement module aggregates edge features weighted by the assigned edge weights, enabling representation of supported structurally ambiguous glycans without selecting a single resolved structure. The model is pretrained on a preprocessed subset of the GlyTouCan1 repository, which contained 253,596 entries before filtering. After excluding entries linked to downstream tasks and applying sequential structural filtering, 167,020 samples remained and were used for pretraining. Pretraining comprised nine self-supervised tasks. Results: Benchmarking on the GlycanML dataset demonstrates that GlycanPUG shows competitive performance relative to GlycanGT across multi-label taxonomy classification and binary immunogenicity prediction. Crucially, on datasets natively containing structural uncertainties (GlyCosmos, GlyConnect), GlycanPUG effectively processes additional structurally ambiguous entries, achieving 83.5% processable coverage across all glycans from all biological sources in GlyCosmos, with taxonomic classification performance (e.g., mean macro F1 of 0.7376 for Domain). Ablation of the node pre-enhancement module reduces macro F1, and post-hoc analysis identifies rank-dependent associations between structural uncertainty and prediction errors. All results reported above are averaged over ten independent random seeds (1-10). Conclusions: GlycanPUG broadens the set of glycans that can be represented while retaining supported structural ambiguities.

items.title: Convergence of Independently Established Oncogenes in a Combined Breast and Ovarian Cancer Model: Hub Gene Validation and identification of potential Food-Derived therapeutics.
items.blurb: Breast and ovarian cancers share molecular alterations that may reveal common therapeutic targets. Here, we integrated six Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets to identify shared transcriptional changes across the two cancers. Independent differential expression analysis followed by direction-specific intersection identified 396 shared differentially expressed genes (DEGs), comprising 192 upregulated and 204 downregulated genes. Protein-protein interaction analysis prioritized ten hub genes: AURKA, AURKB, BCL2, BIRC5, CCNA2, CDK1, FOXO1, KIF11, PTEN, and TOP2A. Functional enrichment highlighted cell-cycle regulation, mitotic spindle organization, and p53-associated signalling. Independent expression assessment using GEPIA2 identified seven hub genes significantly upregulated in both cancers, while FOXO1 was downregulated. Regulatory network analysis further identified candidate transcription factors and miRNAs potentially associated with these hubs. For therapeutic exploration, a 70,478-compound FooDB library was progressively filtered to 233 candidates using physicochemical, structural-alert, machine-learning-based bioactivity, and ADMET criteria. Molecular docking against eight selected druggable hubs, followed by decoy benchmarking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, prioritized three complexes: CDK1-artonin L, AURKB-taraxacin, and KIF11-L-thyronine. CDK1-artonin L demonstrated the strongest overall computational support, whereas the AURKB and KIF11 complexes showed differing levels of binding and energetic evidence. This study provides an integrated multi-cohort framework for identifying shared molecular hubs in breast and ovarian cancer and prioritizing food-derived compounds for further investigation. The findings nominate CDK1, AURKB, and KIF11 for experimental evaluation.

items.title: An AI agent guides a pipeline for selective protein interaction inhibitors from discovery across targets to preclinical evaluation
items.blurb: A protein can engage multiple partners, making it challenging to disrupt disease-associated interactions while preserving others. We developed Bivexia, an AI agent that guides a multistage pipeline from discovery and de novo design through preclinical evaluation. Its decision rules are fixed in advance, and each prospective selection by the agent is cryptographically committed before testing. The objective is to discover small molecules that disrupt specified interactions of a target protein while preserving others. A compound advanced by Bivexia bound LAG-3 with nanomolar affinity and disrupted its interactions with tau and amyloid-{beta} while preserving binding to MHC class II and FGL1. It reduced tau and amyloid-{beta} burden in independent cohorts across two mouse models. The same rules gave three of nine hits on PrP and two of nine on LRP1, none in random controls. Our findings establish a framework for AI agents to pursue defined interaction selectivity across targets.

items.title: BiocPy: A Framework for Cross-Platform Genomic Data andMethods Interoperability
items.blurb: Bioconductor provides standardized data structures and statistical methods for high-throughput genomic analysis in R, whereas Python has become a primary environment for machine learning, image analysis, and general-purpose data science. Combining tools across both ecosystems often requires ad-hoc file conversions or embedded language runtimes that can lose metadata, introduce maintenance overhead, or lead to subtle differences in downstream results. Here, we present BiocPy, a collection of Python packages that support cross-language genomic workflows through three complementary layers: (1) native Python implementations of Bioconductor's core data structures; (2) lossless data exchange via direct reading and writing of serialized R (.rds) objects and the language-neutral ArtifactDB format for persistent, multi-stage pipelines; and (3) a cross-platform method development paradigm built on shared C++ libraries wrapped across R, Python, and WebAssembly to support identical statistical analyses across environments. All packages in the BiocPy ecosystem are published to the Python Package Index (PyPI) with source code hosted at [https://github.com/BiocPy].

items.title: Local wavefront alignment with corrected free-end penalty
items.blurb: Background: Pairwise alignment of nucleotide and protein sequences is a fundamental problem in bioinformatics. Wavefront alignment (WFA) is a groundbreaking algorithmic advance that reduces the time complexity of exact (semi-)global pairwise alignment with affine gap penalties from O(N2) to O(sN). Despite its success, WFA has yet to be extended to the local sequence alignment scope. Results: In this work, we propose a local wavefront alignment (lWFA) which generalizes WFA to the local alignment scope and preserves both the O(sN) time and the O(sN) to O(s2) space complexity. We also propose the bidirectional lWFA (lBiWFA), which reduces the space complexity of lWFA from O(s2) to O(s) while maintaining the time complexity as O(sN). Benchmarks show that lWFA and lBiWFA outperform current exact local alignment libraries like SeqAn and Parasail in aligning long sequences with error rate less than 5%. Conclusions: We suggest to use lBiWFA over lWFA because it has negligible memory footprint for aligning reads up to 20kbp, and is faster than lWFA except for short reads with very low error rates. According to the real-data benchmarks, lBiWFA are faster than SeqAn and Parasail for aligning NGS short reads with 0.1%[~]1% error rate and ONT long reads with 3%[~]5% error rate. However, for reads sequenced by legacy long-read platforms with 10%[~]15% error rate, SeqAn and Parasail are faster. Nevertheless, lBiWFA has a competitive speed for reads with error rate up to 10%. One may choose lBiWFA over SeqAn and Parasail if the memory usage is the major concern.

items.title: CheekAI: An explainable, deep learning epigenetic aging clock based on lifestyle and health epigenetic biomarker proxies
items.blurb: The human methylome is poorly understood and, as such, the vast majority of epigenetic aging clocks are unexplainable black boxes. To address this, we created CheekAI, a robust deep learning model that uses lifestyle and health epigenetic biomarker proxies (EBPs) to predict age. Trained using a longitudinal dataset of 25,400 adult buccal DNA methylation samples derived from 14,716 distinct adults, we used principal components and multi-objective optimization to produce a clock that is explainable, reproducible, responsive, and accurate. The Pearson correlation with chronological age is 0.969, the mean absolute error is 2.49 years, and the intraclass correlation coefficient across 679 replicate pairs is 0.990. CheekAI was significantly associated with a plethora of lifestyle and health variables, including resting heart rate, omega-3 intake, ultra-processed food intake, daily step count, resistance training, and time spent in nature. When applied to external saliva and buccal datasets, CheekAI significantly captured a variety of signals, including smoking and oesophageal cancer. CheekAI was also significantly reduced by a multifactorial lifestyle intervention and this reduction was driven by improvements in dietary and metabolic EBPs. This novel artificial intelligence model represents the first instance of a buccal epigenetic aging clock that utilizes EBPs to offer interpretability and actionability.

items.title: WildTrust-UAV: uncertainty-aware wildlife detection with privacy-preserving spatial disclosure and verifiable inference provenance
items.blurb: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery has made wildlife surveys faster and safer, but a detected animal is not yet a conservation record. Detector confidence scores are often poorly calibrated, exact coordinates of threatened species can expose them to harm, and an observation is rarely tied back to the image, model, and settings that produced it. WildTrust-UAV addresses these three problems in one framework. It pairs a YOLO11 detector with stochastic-view uncertainty estimation, temperature scaling fitted on validation data, a selective gateway that accepts, defers, or rejects each detection, role-based disclosure of animal locations, and a provenance record that hashes the source image, model, configuration, prediction, uncertainty, timestamp, and nonce. Records are aggregated in a Merkle tree and signed with Ed25519 so that any observation can be verified independently. We report three evaluations on the public WAID dataset. In the detection experiment, two YOLO11n runs reached mAP@0.50 of 0.901 and 0.903 and mAP@0.50:0.95 of 0.527 on a 2,000-image held-out test set. In a separate reliability experiment on 122,720 test detections, temperature scaling reduced expected calibration error from 0.0715 to 0.0179 and the Brier score from 0.0353 to 0.0222. Composite uncertainty identified erroneous detections with an AUROC of 0.904, although confidence alone did better (0.992). Deferring the least reliable detections lowered selective risk from 0.722 at near-full coverage to 0.610 at 69.9% coverage, so considerable error remains in the candidate set. In the provenance experiment, the verifier rejected all 4,500 tampered submissions across nine attack scenarios and accepted all 500 genuine controls, with batch construction and signing taking 0.1 to 2.5 ms. Location policies used synthetic coordinates, and the ledger is a local prototype. Calibration and verifiable records can thus be added to a UAV detection pipeline at low cost, while combining uncertainty signals does not automatically improve error detection.

items.title: A Two-Stage YOLO-Swin Transformer Pipeline for Cross-Dataset White Blood Cell Classification
items.blurb: Background: White blood cell (WBC) classification across datasets is challenged by differences in staining, image context, and class distributions. Methods: We developed a two-stage YOLO11-Swin Transformer pipeline. In the first stage, WBC detection and context-preserving cropping, a YOLO11 detector finds the leukocyte in each uncropped image and produces a cell-focused crop that retains the surrounding background. In the second stage, WBC classification, a Swin Transformer (Swin-B) assigns the crop to one of nine cell types. The classifier was trained on detector-cropped cells from five public datasets, so the first stage supplies the same kind of input at test time; morphology-preserving color augmentation addressed staining variation, and class-weighted cross-entropy addressed class imbalance. WBCBench2026, a public benchmark not used for training, served for external evaluation in seven harmonized classes, scored by macro-F1 (the mean of per-class F1). Further analyses removed the first stage or masked the background, compared classifier backbones, held out each training dataset (leave-one-dataset-out, LODO), and tested a second split (Phase-2) with about 60% synthetically degraded images. Results: The full pipeline reached an external macro-F1 of 0.879{+/-}0.006 on 8,080 benchmark images. With uncropped images as input, the same crop-trained classifier reached 0.627{+/-}0.039, and crops that kept the surrounding background outperformed background-masked crops (0.867 versus 0.760). With identical detector-cropped input, Swin-B outperformed convolutional baselines (0.863 versus 0.718-0.813), and its advantage over ResNet50 persisted across three training configurations. In LODO, macro-F1 on the held-out dataset ranged from 0.59 to 0.91, revealing source-specific variation not fully covered by the remaining datasets. On Phase-2, macro-F1 was 0.769{+/-}0.002. Two hematologists independently reviewed all 205 blast- or promyelocyte-related model-benchmark disagreements and gave the same verdict on 73 crops (35.6%): 21 model right, 43 model wrong, 9 ambiguous. Conclusions: The proposed two-stage pipeline achieved strong cross-dataset WBC classification performance. Context-preserving cropping was essential for the crop-trained classifier, and the LODO findings support representing the same classes across diverse sources when developing robust WBC classifiers.

items.title: Beyond screens: a gaze-driven auditory human-computer interface
items.blurb: Brain-computer interfaces enable humans to communicate and manipulate external devices by converting physiological signals into actions. These signals often have a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) too low to enable their use in real-world Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Notably, electrooculography (EOG) measurements of gaze direction exhibit a higher SNR, making them widely employed in HCI applications with displays. Nevertheless, display-free paradigms can also leverage the high SNR of EOG measurements of eye gaze. Current auditory paradigms present options sequentially, extending stimulus presentation time and reducing the information transfer rates (ITRs) compared to visual displays. This paper introduces an HCI approach that combines the SNR of eye gaze with a rapid auditory display paradigm. This paradigm leverages the human capacity to focus on a single auditory stream presented among others. By integrating eye gaze with a rapid auditory display, our method attains average accuracies of 82.7% for a five-option menu and average peak ITRs of 41 bits/min. This increase in performance represents a stride towards practical HCIs in real-world scenarios and display-free smart devices.

items.title: Biophysics-informed generative models improve activity and thermostability of designed ribozymes
items.blurb: Generative models of biological sequences can produce molecules that fold and function similarly to natural ones. A further challenge is to steer generation toward a desired property, such as resistance to high temperature. This is particularly difficult when available sequence data are limited, and typically requires probing thousands of variants experimentally, either through directed evolution or to retrain a model specialized to the targeted property. Ideally, however, one would avoid such an expensive experimental step. Here, we show that biophysical information can complement limited evolutionary data to guide the design of catalytic RNA molecules toward increased activity and thermostability. We combine a sequence generative model with a physical score based on the Turner nearest-neighbor model, whose parameters were originally derived from calorimetric measurements, independently of the sequence family considered. On its own, this physical score is ineffective for design: optimizing it destroys function, likely because it is blind to the catalytic core and to tertiary contacts. However, when coupled to the generative model, it provides complementary information that enables better designs than evolutionary data alone. We demonstrate this on self-splicing group I intron ribozymes: starting from designs that are active at 37 C but inactive at 60 C, fewer than ten substitutions are sufficient to confer catalytic activity at 60 C.

items.title: Engineering Bacteriophages to Overcome Complement-Mediated Neutralization
items.blurb: Bacteriophages (phages) are promising alternatives to antibiotics for treating antibiotic-resistant infections, but their clinical durability is limited by the host immune response against phages. Using phage T4 as a model and both C1q-KO and C3-deficient mice, we show that antibody recognition of phages triggers complement-dependent neutralization and clearance of phage particles in vivo. To mitigate this complement-mediated clearance, we engineer phages to display the complement-modulating Factor H binding peptide, a phage we call T4-FactorH.BP. Indeed, T4-FactorH.BP resists inactivation in human donor sera from individuals with pre-existing antibodies against T4 phage. Similarly, in mice immunized against T4 circulation of T4-FactorH.BP is prolonged in vivo. These results establish a critical role for the classical complement pathway in phage clearance and provide a path towards improving the pharmacokinetics of phage therapeutics in vivo by evading complement.

items.title: Rigid granular scaffolds reveal transcriptional responses to cellular confinement
items.blurb: A large variety of cells migrate through confined spaces in vivo, where mechanical confinement influences their fate and function. However, existing in vitro confinement models are low-throughput, limiting discovery of confinement-responsive genes and recovery of confined cells. Here, we present non-annealed glass microparticle scaffolds (GlaMS) as a scalable, high-throughput 3D confinement system with interconnected voids that mimic physiological confinement while enabling efficient cell retrieval. Using LOVAMAP, a computational tool that segments void spaces to estimate spatial constrictions, we quantified confinement levels in GlaMS and compared them with ex vivo interstitial spaces to identify the sphere size that best mimics in vivo confinement. Using human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) as a mechanosensitive cell model, confinement within GlaMS was found to induce morphological changes, accelerated migration, altered YAP signaling, and enhanced osteogenic priming after replating, demonstrating transient confinement-induced effects. Taking advantage of the high throughput capabilities of GlaMS, we performed RNAseq on populations of confined cells and identified confinement degree-dependent shifts in gene expression. TMEM158 emerged as a previously unrecognized confinement-sensitive gene, was independently validated in microchannel assays, and was found by loss-of-function analysis to contribute to efficient confined migration. Together, this work establishes GlaMS as a scalable platform for population-level confinement mechanobiology, allowing recovery and molecular profiling of cells exposed to predictable three-dimensional confinement.

items.title: Albumin alleviates pressure overload-induced heart failure by improving mitochondrial homeostasis via PKA-LKB1-AMPK axis
items.blurb: Aims Heart failure (HF) is a global health challenge due to its high incidence, mortality, and socioeconomic burden. Despite medical advancements, HF prognosis remains poor, highlighting the need for enhanced understanding and treatment strategies. Serum albumin, a key circulatory protein, has gained attention as a biomarker in cardiovascular diseases. Low serum albumin levels are linked to HF incidence, progression, and prognosis, suggesting its regulatory role, though mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the role of serum albumin in HF pathogenesis and investigate its potential therapeutic effects. Methods and results A mouse model of pressure overload-induced HF was established via transverse aortic constriction (TAC). Serum albumin levels were significantly decreased in HF mice. Administration of recombinant mouse serum albumin (rMSA) effectively restored serum albumin concentrations, improved cardiac systolic function, alleviated cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis, and reduced inflammatory responses, collectively attenuating disease progression. In contrast, albumin-knockout (Alb-/-, AKO) HF mice displayed aggravated pathological manifestations compared with wild-type (WT) controls, whereas rMSA supplementation markedly ameliorated these impairments. In vitro experiments demonstrated that rMSA protected against phenylephrine (PE)-induced hypertrophy in cardiomyocytes. To elucidate the underlying mechanism, transcriptomic analyses of cardiac tissues revealed that albumin played a critical role in improving mitochondrial homeostasis. Experimental validation further demonstrated that albumin activated the PKA-LKB1-AMPK signaling axis, leading to improved mitochondrial respiratory function and oxidative phosphorylation, as well as enhanced mitochondrial quality control. These changes promoted fatty acid oxidation and optimized energy metabolism, thereby reversing the energy imbalance underlying cardiac dysfunction. Conclusion Our study suggests that serum albumin exerts a protective effect in HF by improving mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolism disorders, thus reversing energy imbalance and mitigating disease progression. These results support recombinant serum albumin as a promising therapeutic for HF, with its mechanism involving the critical improvement of mitochondrial homeostasis.

items.title: Effective control of treadmilling filaments by plus-end capping
items.blurb: Bacterial cell division depends on the tubulin homolog FtsZ, which assembles into a membrane-bound cytokinetic Z-ring. FtsZ filaments treadmill, growing at one end and shrinking at the other, and many regulatory proteins control where and when the Z-ring forms. Whether treadmilling itself confers a regulatory advantage, and how inhibitors exploit it, has remained unclear. Here we show that the Escherichia coli nucleoid occlusion factor SlmA caps the growing ends of treadmilling FtsZ filaments, converting steady-state subunit turnover into net filament shrinkage. Using in vitro reconstitution of membrane-bound FtsZ filaments with quantitative fluorescence and single-molecule imaging, we find that SlmA shortens filaments and reduces polymer mass at concentrations far below that of FtsZ, behaving like the bona fide capper FtsZ L272E. Structural prediction and mutagenesis identify a previously unrecognized interface between SlmA and the polymerization-competent surface of FtsZ that is required for activity in vitro and in vivo and that acts together with the known FtsZ C-terminal peptide contact. A minimal stochastic model shows why end capping outperforms sequestration and severing, establishing kinetic asymmetry as a general point of control for treadmilling cytoskeletal polymers.

items.title: FiberTron enables regulatory variant effect prediction and testing from multi-omic long reads of a single sample
items.blurb: State-of-the-art sequence-to-function models are trained on large compendia of public data to predict regulatory activity across hundreds of cell types. However, they are not designed to interpret individual genomes, effects in under-sampled cell types, or provide a comprehensive view of how genetic variation influences complex diseases. Here we show that a single sample profiled with Fiber-seq and Nanopore direct RNA-seq contains enough information to train such a model from scratch. FiberTron, a 12M parameter convolutional-transformer model, takes 524 kb of reference sequence and predicts CpG methylation, chromatin accessibility and strand-specific transcript coverage at base-pair resolution (median Pearson's r of 0.85-0.97 on held-out chromosomes). Trained in under a day on a single four-GPU node, our HG002 model performs on par with models such as AlphaGenome on dsQTL and eQTL variant effect prediction tasks, despite being over an order of magnitude smaller. As training uses reference sequence only, each sample's phased multi-omic long reads remain available to test its variant-effect predictions. FiberTron recapitulates OAS1 splicing variation associated with COVID-19 risk, recovers 79% of allele-specific accessibility variants in a melanoma line, identifies oncogenic TERT promoter and TAL1 enhancer mutations, and predicts EWSR1::ATF1 fusion transcript expression and its unique chromatin imprint in a rare clear cell sarcoma patient sample. Lightweight single-sample training brings base-resolution interpretation of non-coding variation within reach of individual laboratories.

items.title: Divergent immune trajectories distinguish resistance and susceptibility to bacterial leaf streak in wheat
items.blurb: Bacterial leaf streak (BLS) is an increasingly important disease affecting several cereal crops. The mechanisms linking quantitative trait loci for resistance to downstream immune response against BLS in wheat remain poorly understood. Here, we developed a chromosome-scale genome assembly of the BLS resistant cultivar Boost. With de novo annotation of Boost and Timstein (susceptible cultivar) assemblies, we established a cultivar-resolved framework for dissecting BLS resistance. Both cultivars encoded highly similar immune receptor repertoires, but the major resistance locus, QBls.fcu-3B.1, comprised a divergent receptor kinase haplotype with extensive structural variations, divergent tandem receptor arrays, and constitutively elevated expression of multiple receptor kinases in the resistant cultivar. Candidate receptor kinases in Boost exhibited conserved intracellular kinase domains but substantial divergence among extracellular recognition domains relative to their syntenic homologs in Timstein. Dual reference transcriptome analyses at 24, 48, and 96 hours after inoculation (HAI) revealing contrasting immune trajectories in resistant and susceptible cultivars. Boost progressed through a focused signaling transition at 48 HAI, followed by coordinated activation of several defense modules, such as antimicrobial metabolism, cell wall reinforcement, transcriptional regulation, and immune homeostasis. In contrast, the susceptible cultivar underwent coordinated repression of these defense-related modules together with chromatin-associated transcriptional changes and induction of host transcriptional machinery during disease establishment. Our findings suggest that quantitative resistance to BLS is associated not simply with immune receptor composition, but also with constitutive immune surveillance and temporal coordination of downstream defense, providing a putative mechanistic framework linking natural genomic variations to quantitative BLS resistance in wheat.

items.title: Pharmacogenomic diversity at tuberculosis-treatment loci across African populations: phased haplotypes, regulatory architecture and NAT2 acetylator inference
items.blurb: Background: Tuberculosis imposes a major public-health burden in Africa, while variation in isoniazid and rifampicin disposition creates opportunities for improved pharmacotherapy. The population architecture of extended, phased pharmacogenomic backgrounds remains less well characterized than individual marker frequencies. Methods: We analyzed high-coverage, phased GRCh38 genomes from 661 unrelated individuals sampled from five continental-African and two African-diaspora populations at NAT2, SLCO1B1, CES2, HLA-B, NR1I2 and UGT1A1. We integrated frequency differentiation, reduced phased signatures, linkage disequilibrium, functional annotation and NAT2 core-allele inference with individual-clustered permutation tests. Results: The six loci contributed 17,223 annotated variant records and 276 entries in a capped frequency-differentiation register. Exact NAT2 core-definition matching was achieved for 1,321/1,322 chromosomes (99.92%), and determinate genotype-inferred acetylator categories for 620/661 individuals (93.80%). Among the sampled continental-African populations, 35-site noncore background distributions differed within NAT2 *5 (BH-adjusted q=0.000100), *4 (q=0.024733) and *6 (q=0.000350) groups. Distinct phased and linkage architectures also characterized transporter, hydrolysis, regulatory and HLA-B genomic regions. Conclusion: African population-associated variation extends beyond commonly used pharmacogenetic allele definitions. The observed NAT2 backgrounds and complementary locus signatures provide a foundation for targeted molecular studies and prospective pharmacokinetic validation that could inform future population-responsive TB treatment research.

items.title: Diversity of Environmental and Genome-Associated Eukaryotic Circular Rep-Encoding Single-Stranded DNA Viruses
items.blurb: Circular Rep-encoding single-stranded (CRESS) DNA viruses are widespread across diverse environments, yet their genomic diversity, evolutionary relationships, and associations with eukaryotic hosts remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the evolutionary diversity of CRESS DNA viruses by integrating replication-associated protein (Rep) sequences from environmental viral metagenomes, publicly available viral references, and endogenous viral elements (EVEs) identified in fungal and algal genomes. Genome-wide screening revealed numerous EVEs distributed across diverse fungal and algal lineages, highlighting the potential historical associations between CRESS DNA viruses and eukaryotic hosts. Phylogenetic analyses revealed considerable diversity among CRESS DNA viruses, including sequences that could not be assigned to currently recognized viral families. Yet, several of these unclassified sequences formed well-supported monophyletic clades, suggesting that existing taxonomic classifications may require further revision. Furthermore, phylogenetic relationships within and among established viral families suggest that existing taxonomic boundaries may not fully capture the evolutionary diversity of these viruses. The phylogenetic placement of fungal and algal EVEs alongside environmental and reference viral sequences further provides insights into the evolutionary relationships between CRESS DNA viruses and eukaryotic genomes. Collectively, our findings expand the known evolutionary diversity of CRESS DNA viruses, identify distinct viral lineages requiring further taxonomic evaluation, and provide a framework for investigating their genomic evolution, taxonomic relationships, and associations with eukaryotic hosts.

items.title: No evidence of evolution of male fitness components in response to yeast deprivation: Putative female specific nutrient dependent reproductive adaptation
items.blurb: Intersexual genetic correlation (IGC) is pervasive in sexually reproducing organisms and can constrain sex-specific adaptive evolution. Nevertheless, sexes frequently undergo adaptive divergence in response to novel ecological challenges. Here, we investigated whether adaptation to nutritional stress is sex-limited or constrained by shared genetic architecture. We utilized four laboratory-adapted populations of Drosophila melanogaster subjected to experimental evolution under adult-stage live-yeast deprivation for over 140 generations - a regime that previously drove adaptive female reproductive evolution, particularly enhancing early-life fecundity and ovarian function. Because female D. melanogaster rely heavily on dietary yeast for protein-dependent egg production, this evolutionary response may be female-limited. Alternatively, male fitness traits could respond either through direct selection or via correlated response driven by IGC. To distinguish between these hypotheses, we evaluated a comprehensive suite of pre- and post-copulatory male competitive fitness components. We found that all measured male fitness traits remained unchanged following experimental evolution, demonstrating that nutrient-dependent adaptation in these populations is strictly female-specific, with no evidence of correlated responses or sexually antagonistic trade-offs. Our results indicate that the genetic architecture underlying nutrient-dependent reproductive adaptation is largely decoupled between the sexes, allowing each sex to independently approach its sex-specific fitness optimum.

items.title: Historical overestimated abundance of a Critically Endangered species: the case of the tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) of Mindoro Island
items.blurb: Population abundance is a central parameter in conservation, for which biased estimates can seriously undermine management strategies for threatened species. The tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) is a Critically Endangered large herbivore endemic to Mindoro Island, Philippines. The species has been monitored annually at Mounts Iglit-Baco Natural Park (MIBNP) since 2000 using a multi-vantage-point count method that is prone to both imperfect detection and repeated counting of the same individuals across sessions. Because the historical abundance estimation is an index of relative abundance with no probabilistic modeling of counts, the actual number of tamaraw in what is considered as the largest remaining population is still poorly known. To fill this gap, we conducted an independent double-observer experiment over five years (2022-2026) and fitted Bayesian hierarchical detection models to the counts. As expected, detection probability was <1 throughout (single-observer estimates 0.41-0.84; combined-observer 0.68-0.96), confirming that a substantial fraction of animals is missed by rangers during all counts. Compared with these estimates, historical counts overestimated tamaraw abundance by a factor of 1.61-2.34, yielding a mean population size across 2022-2026 of 203 individuals (95% credible interval 182-226) rather than the roughly 400-500 individuals previously assumed. Our results imply that the MIBNP tamaraw population, while more vulnerable to demographic and genetic risks than previously believed, has likely responded positively to ongoing conservation efforts; we recommend that population viability assessments and translocation plans for the species be revised accordingly.

items.title: Apple floral attractants function across the 24-hour cycle to support potential diurnal and nocturnal pollinators
items.blurb: Pollination in apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) is typically attributed to diurnal bees, yet nocturnal insects also contribute to fruit set. To assess whether apple flowers recruit potential pollinators throughout the 24-hour cycle, we quantified diel patterns in floral attractants and insect visitation in an orchard in Northwest Arkansas, United States. We measured nectar and volatiles and used a combination of visual surveys, light traps, and video recordings to assess insect abundance and floral visitation while controlling for weather conditions. We found that nectar volume remained consistent across sampling times, indicating that reward availability is dielly stable. Floral volatile bouquets, in contrast, exhibited subtle but significant diel and interannual variation, driven largely by shifts in aldehydes, alkanes, and benzenoids. Several compounds associated with nocturnal moth and dipteran attraction - including alpha-farnesene, benzyl alcohol, and aldehydes - were enriched at night. Apple flowers were visited by insects around the clock. Nighttime visitors were less abundant than daytime visitors but taxonomically diverse, including moths and nematoceran flies, whereas bees, wasps, and brachyceran flies were restricted to daytime. Different taxonomic groups therefore alternated over the diel cycle, producing pronounced shifts in visitor community composition. Thus, apple flowers produce attractants across the diel cycle and nocturnal insects - particularly dipterans and moths - are a consistent, ecologically meaningful component of the apple flower-visiting assemblage. Our findings support the need for pollinator-inclusive management that accounts for the full diel cycle, particularly when scheduling pesticide applications near bloom, to sustain diverse pollinator communities and enhance the resilience of apple production systems.

items.title: The use of cultured symbionts enhances the survival of reef-deployed coral recruits
items.blurb: Introduction: Symbiodiniaceae dinoflagellates are essential for coral juvenile development and survival, yet early-life symbiont provisioning remains underused in coral restoration. Objectives: We tested whether inoculating sexually propagated Acropora spathulata recruits with cultured symbionts before reef deployment improves survival and shapes symbiont community composition. Methods: Recruits inoculated with cultured Cladocopium sp. (C1) or Durusdinium trenchii (D1), and uninoculated recruits (Control) were deployed on the central Great Barrier Reef. Results: Both inoculation treatments approximately doubled survival relative to Control, although the benefit varied with local benthic habitat. C1 and D1 recruits were dominated by symbiont sequences matching their respective inoculated cultures, while Control recruits predominantly harboured a Durusdinium-dominant community closely resembling the cultured D1. Cultured C1 was also dominant among most C1-inoculated recruits after nine months, although some diverged from the inoculated community towards a mixed assemblage with Durusdinium. Conclusions: Similar survival benefits in the two inoculation treatments suggest that the timing and success of symbiont establishment were more critical for early survival than symbiont genus identity, under the conditions and period of this study.

items.title: Electron microscopy reveals the headquarters of poxviruses
items.blurb: Mpox remains a smoldering threat, with recent clusters in Brazil, Thailand and Austria and ongoing hot spots across multiple African countries. Other poxviruses also endanger human or animal health. A new study by the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) uncovers the inner workings of the poxvirus core: how its gene-copying machines sit parked in dormant pairs, ready to print viral instructions and release them into the host cell through dedicated export portals embedded in the core shell.

items.title: Consumers, oblivious of being targeted, find online ads helpful
items.blurb: Most online shoppers know that ads strategically follow them across sites, a mechanism known as "ad retargeting." A new study led by Penn State researchers found that consumers find these targeted ads helpful, but explaining why they are seeing an ad can backfire by increasing concerns about being watched.

items.title: NASA spacecraft data reveal how solar system's tail shifts over 14 years
items.blurb: A Southwest Research Institute-led study is the first to map out the distinct motion paths of the heliotail lobes across a 14-year period using data from NASA's Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) spacecraft. By identifying the paths followed by these lobes, the study provides a better understanding of how solar activity shapes the heliotail.

items.title: Physics-guided AI reconstructs fluid flow from sparse, noisy data
items.blurb: Medical imaging technologies have transformed how scientists and physicians visualize blood flowing through the human heart, but even the most advanced imaging techniques cannot capture every detail of fluid motion. Researchers at the University of California, Irvine, have developed a computational approach that combines fundamental physics with artificial intelligence to reconstruct a more complete and accurate picture of fluid flow from limited and imperfect measurements.

items.title: Earth's core may be leaking a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
items.blurb: Scientists have discovered an unusual carbon signature in Hawaiian volcanic rocks that suggests some of Earth's carbon originated in ancient meteorites and later escaped from deep within the planet's core. The discovery raises an astonishing possibility: Carbon essential to life may have traveled from space to Earth's depths before emerging through volcanoes billions of years later.

items.title: COP31 went down in flames over fossil fuels — it sends an important message
items.blurb: Nature, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03827-0 Nature reporter James Dinneen reflects on the first international climate summit to collapse since 2009.

items.title: LPMOcat: an interactive database for comparative structural analysis of lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases
items.blurb: LPMOcat is a comprehensive resource of 161 characterised lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs) from all eight CAZy families, in which an automated pipeline integrates data from public databases and, based on a structural alignment, annotates common structural features of LPMOs (e.g. histidine brace, second-sphere residues, loop regions), and calculates per-residue properties (e.g. flexibility, hydrophobicity, hole-hopping pathways). The web application summarises all the gathered information in plots integrated with a similarity tree and allows users to filter the catalogue and compare any set of LPMOs to investigate their structure-function relationships.

items.title: Ancestral and derived feeding morphology during rapid ecological divergence within a species
items.blurb: Derived characters that may have emerged via positive selection can be identified by comparing species, but also possibly subgroups within species. Allopatric and sympatric polymorphism observed in many salmonids is thought to emerge mainly in landlocked populations, which have lost the anadromous lifestyle of their ancestors. Populations of Arctic charr (Salvelinus alpinus) are an example of such polymorphism, commonly diverging along a pelagic-benthic axis. Populations of Icelandic charr can be anadromous or landlocked, like in Lake Thingvallavatn where four morphs coexist differing in habitat use, preferred prey and external feeding morphology. Three of these morphs are also caught in the neighboring Lake Ulfljotsvatn, despite prey availability in the two lakes differing notably. We studied variation of craniofacial morphology in Icelandic charr populations and compared the ecologically specialized sympatric morphs to five anadromous charr populations and to two non-specialized lake populations, as well as across two connected lakes. The results indicate minor variation among anadromous populations and that the benthic lake forms are derived. There was clear phenotypic difference between benthic and pelagic morphs within Thingvallavatn but no differences between the morphs in Ulfljotsvatn. Patterns of variation between corresponding morphs across the two lakes suggest genetics separation and phenotypic plasticity.

items.title: Differential population declines across migratory strategies are shifting European bird communities towards residency
items.blurb: Previous studies revealed steep declines in populations of common migratory birds across Europe, especially for long-distance migrants. However, these studies focussed on continental-scale patterns, and they assigned a single migratory strategy to each species, often not distinguishing short-distance migrants from residents. It thus remains unclear whether the same patterns are found across European countries, and whether they hold when taking into account the variation in migratory behaviour observed across the European populations of many species. Here, we examine how European breeding landbird communities have varied according to migratory strategy between 1990 and 2023, at both continental and national scales. By compiling multiple sources of information on seasonal movements, we characterise the migratory strategy of landbird populations per country (long-distance migrant, short-distance migrant or resident). We combined these data with estimates of population trends and of abundance from national monitoring schemes to quantify changes in both multi-species indices (average change across species) and total abundance of birds, for each migratory strategy. At the continental scale, multi-species indices reveal a strong decline in long-distance migrants (-26.8% between 1990 and 2023), whereas short-distance migrants declined more slowly (-4.5%) and residents remained stable. Changes in total abundance show even steeper declines - of 29.9% and 10.2% for, respectively, long- and short-distance migrants - whereas residents increased slightly (+3.4%). Together, these results point to a gradual reorganisation of bird communities towards a greater dominance of resident birds across Europe. However, these changes are not happening homogenously across the continent: whereas in Central and Southern Europe we observed the same general pattern of declining migrants while residents remained broadly stable or increased, in Northern Europe we reveal declines for all migratory strategies. Overall, our study highlights the widespread vulnerability of migratory birds in Europe, while showing that the reorganisation of bird communities follows different trajectories across regions.

items.title: Normalised whole-plant water supply declines with plant height across the seed-plant phylogeny
items.blurb: Whole-plant water-transport capacity largely controls terrestrial water fluxes, yet it is unresolved to what extent its variation across the seed-plant phylogeny is structured by shared ancestry, edaphoclimatic conditions, plant height or water relation traits. We fitted a phylogenetic structural equation model to maximum leaf-specific whole-plant hydraulic conductance (kL), together with concurrent Huber value (Hv), stomatal conductance (gs), and height for 263 species spanning the global climate space, partitioning direct from indirect effects, and phylogenetically conserved from independent effects. kL declined with height, and Hv did not offset this decline. Hv raised kL but was unrelated to height among species. kL was lower in wetter niches, despite higher Hv there, indicating lower conductance per unit sapwood area. kL was tightly coupled to gs in both conserved and independent variation, so the height-driven decline in kL propagated to gas exchange. Plant height therefore constrains whole-plant hydraulic supply and, through it, gs.

items.title: Monolayer, Spheroid, and Organoid Formats Elicit Proteomic States that Couple Organelle Organization to Metabolic Vulnerabilities
items.blurb: Three-dimensional (3D) cell culture systems are becoming more widely applied to model tissue organization, disease progression, and therapeutic response. Yet, the molecular characteristics that distinguish organoids and spheroids from conventional monolayer culture are incompletely defined. Here, using tumorigenic organoid models of high-grade serous tubo-ovarian cancer (HGSC), we establish a quantitative proteomic resource that reveals how cell architecture and media independently but jointly shape the cellular state in organoids, spheroids, and monolayers. We further pursue HGSC subtype-enriched features within this framework and identify that a poor prognosis-associated genotype with reported paclitaxel hypersensitivity, Trp53-/-;Pten-/-;Nf1-/- (PPN), is marked by increased microtubule-associated proteins, lipid-associated factors, and mitochondrial remodeling. PPN cells displayed clustered lipid droplets, whereby mitochondria-ER tethering increased. Relative to Trp53-/- (P) and a frequent HGSC genotype, Trp53-/-;Brca1+/-;MycOE (PBM), live-cell imaging showed that PPN exhibits the highest degree of stable mitochondria-ER encapsulations, coincident with fission-biased mitochondria and a high-flux respiratory state. Disruption of the mitochondria-ER contact protein PTPIP51 reduced lipid droplet clustering in the PPN state. Because cytomegalovirus is known to exploit host mitochondria remodeling, mitochondria-ER contacts, and metabolic output during infection, we tested whether this pre-existing host configuration is associated with cytomegalovirus permissiveness. PPN organoids exhibited greater murine cytomegalovirus infection and infectious output than matched monolayers or PBM. Together, these data define a resource of distinct protein characteristics between matched monolayer, spheroid, and organoid systems that should be considered for experimental design. We also uncover a mechanistic axis connecting 3D architecture, organelle contacts, metabolism, drug response, and viral permissiveness.

items.title: A multi-scale forecasting framework to prioritize clinically-relevant antibiotic resistance alleles
items.blurb: Established in vitro measures for the emergence of antimicrobial resistance, a critical global threat, can fail to predict which in vitro discovered mutations will dominate in the real world following widespread antibiotic use. Here, we introduce a multi-scale computational framework integrating genetic constraints and population pharmacokinetics and apply it to explain resistance allele success in Acinetobacter baumannii for the historic case of resistance to the fluoroquinolone antibiotic ciprofloxacin. By coupling intrinsic nucleotide substitution likelihoods with continuous-time stochastic modeling under fluctuating drug exposures, our framework clearly prioritizes the most common real world gyrA fluoroquinolone resistance allele S81L over rarer alleles, reflecting its clinical success. While gyrA serves as a proof-of-concept case study for direct, active-site drug-target interactions where the target space is constrained, we observe that the nucleotide substitution likelihoods are not explaining allele success in resistance-determining genes pmrB and adeS. Furthermore, "virtual twin" cohort simulations reveal that restricted drug penetration or compromised immunity expands selective windows, rescuing rare, low-fitness alleles. This advances our understanding of prospective, model-informed risk prediction during antibiotic development.

items.title: Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., novel taxa isolated from figs (Ficus)
items.blurb: Two bacterial strains, WOUb02T and WOUb67T, were isolated from fresh figs (Ficus spp.) collected from the island of Taiwan. Cells of WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Gram-stain-negative rods. Strain WOUb02T was non-motile, whereas WOUb67T exhibited motility. Physiologically, both strains grew optimally at 0.5% (w/v) NaCl and pH 8.0; WOUb02T grew optimally at 37{degrees}C, whereas WOUb67T grew optimally at 30{degrees}C. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the closest relatives to strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Klebsiella terrigena ATCC 33257T (98.2%) and Pseudomonas putida NBRC 14164T (99.9%) respectively. Subsequent phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences revealed that strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T formed distinct lineages within the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively. Further genomic analyses revealed that WOUb02T and WOUb67T shared average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values <95.0% and <70.0%, below the currently accepted thresholds for species-level delineation. Based on phenotypic and genotypic data, strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T could be distinguished from other species with validly published names and are considered to represent novel species in the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively, for which the names Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., are proposed. The type strains are WOUb02T (=NRRL-B 65719T =CCUG 77855T) and WOUb67T (=NRRL-B 65720T =CCUG 77856T).

items.title: Effect of Moisture Content of Paddy (Phka Rumduol) on the Quality of White Rice (Oryza sativa L.)
items.blurb: This study evaluated the impact of paddy moisture content on the quality parameters of white rice produced from Cambodia's premium fragrant variety, Phka Rumduol (Oryza sativa L.). A completely randomized design (CRD) was employed to evaluate the effect of moisture content on rice quality. Paddy samples were adjusted to four target moisture levels (10%, 12%, 14%, and 16%) and subsequently milled under controlled conditions. The CRD ensured unbiased allocation of samples across all treatments, minimizing experimental error during both moisture conditioning and milling processes. The results showed that moisture content had a significant effect (p < 0.05) on all measured quality parameters. Paddy at 14% moisture content produced the best results, with a head rice yield of 63.46 %, and a broken rice percentage of only 4.86 %. Grain appearance was also well preserved, with rice bran yield of 10.67 %, rice husk yield of 18.52 %, and yellow kernels averaging just 0.79 %. In contrast, moisture levels below 12% increased kernel brittleness, leading to breakage rates as high as 26.28 %, while levels above 16% caused grain deformation and discoloration. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining paddy moisture at 14% prior to milling to optimize recovery and preserve the high quality of Phka Rumduol rice. The study provides practical guidance for Cambodian rice processors aiming to improve product quality and strengthen competitiveness in international markets.

items.title: Molecular dynamics simulations and in vivo binding studies indicate distinct membrane binding modes of plant lipid droplet proteins including binding via a hydrophobic face
items.blurb: Plant lipid droplets (LDs) are specialized cellular subcompartments for lipid storage and key hubs for lipid metabolism. They have a unique structure: a hydrophobic core composed of neutral lipids enclosed by a phospholipid monolayer and associated proteins. Progress has been made in the identification and characterization of LD-associated plant proteins in recent years, raising the question of how these proteins bind to LDs. To investigate common structural features of LD association, we set up an in silico system using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the nature of this interaction and to identify predicted binding regions of selected proteins. We then tested the importance of these regions for LD association by transient expression of truncated or mutated variants in tobacco pollen tubes. With this combined approach, we investigated the LD targeting region of thirteen LD-associated proteins. In several proteins, a distinct structural feature, a hydrophobic face, binds to LDs by interacting with the acyl chains of the phospholipid monolayer through large hydrophobic residues thereby pushing the headgroups to the sides. We also analyzed proteins previously assayed for LD association and demonstrate a correlation between predicted binding parameters and in vivo binding.

items.title: Mitochondrial H2S and cytochrome c coordinate guard cell redox dynamics during stomatal immunity
items.blurb: Stomatal pores modulate gas exchange between plants and the environment and are the first layer of defense against pathogens entry. Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a recognized component of the signalling network in guard cells that control stomatal responses. We previously showed that the mitochondrial H2S source {beta}-cyanoalanine synthase (CAS-C1) is required for flg22-induced stomatal closure. Using genetically encoded redox biosensors in Arabidopsis thaliana guard cells, we found that the mitochondrially-targeted H2S donor AP39 and the pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP) flg22 both increased mitochondrial H2O2 within 5 min, while the flg22-triggered rise was attenuated in cas-c1 mutants. Dissipating the mitochondrial membrane potential ({Delta}{psi}m) with the uncoupler 2,4-dinitrophenol prevented both mitochondrial oxidation and stomatal closure. Cytochrome c (CYTc), the mobile electron carrier between complexes III and IV, proved essential for this pathway. CYTc-deficient lines showed a stomatal response similar than wild-type (wt) to ABA and light but failed to trigger stomatal closure upon exposure to different PAMPs. In these plants, neither AP39 nor flg22 induced guard cell mitochondrial hyperpolarization or an increase in cytosolic H2O2. By the dimedone-switch method, we show that CYTc is persulfidated in vivo, identifying this respiratory protein as a target of H2S-mediated posttranslational modification. At the whole-plant level, cytc plants were more susceptible to spray inoculation with Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato hrcC- at early stages of infection. Together, these results position CYTc as a mitochondrial node that links H2S signalling to guard cell redox dynamics during stomatal immunity.

items.title: Species turnover dominates plant trait variation along continental climate gradients
items.blurb: Variation in plant functional traits along climate gradients chiefly arises from two processes: turnover of species with different trait values, and trait adjustment within species across environments. Yet, the relative contributions of these processes remain poorly quantified, limiting our ability to predict how traits, species distributions and, in turn, ecosystem properties will respond to climate change. Across seven functional traits and 1867 plant taxa from continental Australia, we provide a unified assessment of among- versus within-species contributions across multiple dimensions of plant function. Species turnover emerged as the dominant process driving trait variation along both precipitation and temperature gradients. Nevertheless, the contribution of within-species adjustment to climate differed substantially among traits and was generally greater in non-woody than woody taxa, these patterns being most clearly expressed along precipitation gradients. Our findings imply that plant traits will track changing climatic conditions primarily through species replacement, particularly for traits such as wood density and seed mass. Species may also respond in situ through adjustments in leaf physiology and morphology and, in woody taxa, through shifts in relative allocation between leaves and stem tissues. This knowledge has potential to improve predictions of the structure and function of future plant communities.

items.title: Hexed review – Disney’s witchy caper is a wicked disappointment
items.blurb:
A teen girl discovers she is a witch in this mostly magic-free reminder that original animation is stuck in an unoriginal place

As bleak as Disney’s overreliance on sequels might have become, it’s not quite as bleak as the crumbling state of its original output. Obviously because of the former, the latter category has become that much less populated but even when the studio has recently bothered to release something without a number in the title, it’s been hard to really see the point.

With or without Pixar, films like Elio, Strange World, Raya and the Last Dragon, Luca, Elemental, Onward and Wish have all felt as uninspired as something a rival might try to desperately cobble together in an attempt to lure kids away from Disney. Three Thanksgivings ago, Wish was a particularly poor yet extremely smug example of how rubbishy things have got, a personality-free princess tale that doubled up as a 100-year anniversary victory lap. It was Disney’s worst-reviewed animated film in almost two decades and its deserved box office failure cost about $131m. Unperturbed, its co-director Fawn Veerasunthorn (along with Moana 2 director Jason Hand) is back this holiday with another rote rip-off adventure that doesn’t deserve its place in the kingdom.

Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch of all time, and is likely to become the biggest video game of all time. It’s a once-in-a-lifetime event, a phenomenon that will shape games as a medium and pop culture at large for years to come, set against the backdrop of its developers fighting for their rights at studio Rockstar Games. It has snatched sales and streaming records and become the best-reviewed game ever (pulling ahead of 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time). It’s also the first GTA game with a female protagonist, who also happens to be a woman of colour. Yet very few women (and seemingly no women of colour) played and reviewed it before release.

When GTA VI’s review embargo lifted on 18 November, the gender imbalance was immediately obvious. Out of 156 reviewers, only six appeared to be women. As journalist Lex Luddy noted in a BlueSky post, that is 3.8%.

The US and the UK had been publicly warning their allies for weeks about what Russia was planning, as well as threatening the Russians with a wave of sanctions unprecedented against a major power.

Putin’s foreign policy had long relied on confusion and untruth. By saying that they knew exactly what he was up to, Britain and America were hoping first to deny him his usual ambiguity, and second to pressure the men around him into making him stop, since war would deprive them of the stolen assets they’d stashed in London’s most exclusive neighbourhoods.

items.title: The Song of Stork and Dromedary by Anjet Daanje review – don’t miss this glorious epic inspired by Emily Brontë
items.blurb:
The afterlife of a Yorkshire village girl who becomes a gothic literary icon is explored across three centuries, in a thrilling paean to the power of books

I had a plan. I was going to nibble away at this great wedge of a book, a morsel a night, like a little reading mouse. But then the story swallowed me whole. I read Dutch author Anjet Daanje’s The Song of Stork and Dromedary over three feverish nights, and spent the days in between longing for the dark. This 720-page novel should come with a warning label: may cause severe infatuation.

We begin in the fictional Yorkshire village of Bridge Fowling with Susan Knowles-Chester, a woman who attends to the dead. The year is 1847, and Susan knows the old ways, the threshold rituals: how to arrange a corpse so it doesn’t gape and gawp at the living. “The villagers have a horror of her work, for wherever she goes, she leaves grief like driftwood in her wake, yet when the time comes, many ask for her help, it is an open secret.”

items.title: A year of deadly floods and fires – and yet Cop31 still collapsed. When will our leaders grasp the scale of this crisis? | Bill McGuire
items.blurb:
Fossil fuel producers are choking off progress while we reap the whirlwind of our inaction. This is what sleepwalking to disaster looks like

It’s sometimes said that we are sleepwalking into climate catastrophe. But the reality is that we are walking into it with our eyes wide open, in the full knowledge that we are dooming the lives of our children, and countless generations down the line, to hell on Earth. In the UK, summer temperatures could hit the mid-40s within decades, making extreme drought and harvest failures the norm, and leaving people camping in the streets as houses become overheated death traps. Across Europe, the fastest-heating continent on the planet, the 50C temperature record could be broken as soon as next year. Elsewhere, by 2050, humid heatwaves could take many thousands of lives in a single day in parts of China, South Asia and the Gulf region.

We continue to pump out the CO2 weight-equivalent of 800,000 Titanics every year, with no end in sight. Meanwhile the latest climate Cop – the only global initiative with the potential to turn things around – has just collapsed in disarray, unable to get its act together even to agree on a vague form of words about the need to transition away from fossil fuels.

Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news

  • Republican senators criticize Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang


The surge in stock markets since Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia was announced shows that investors are “willing to re-engage with the AI theme when uncertainty recedes”, says Christian Stocker, lead equity strategist for UniCredit Munich.

But… Stocker argues that the rally reflected relief that the AI supply chain and investment cycle are unlikely to be abruptly disrupted, rather than renewed conviction that all concerns have disappeared.

Questions about financing structures, profitability and the ultimate returns on AI spending remain largely unresolved.

In other words, the debate has shifted. Investors are no longer asking whether AI investment will continue. They are increasingly asking whether the path from investment to monetisation will be slower, more uneven and more dependent on favourable financing conditions than previously assumed. Recent market volatility suggests that the AI narrative remains intact, but the market is becoming less willing to assume a straight-line path to future earnings growth.

With fears of an AI slowdown receding, it also led markets to price back in a more hawkish path for the Federal Reserve over the months ahead.

So for the next meeting in December, markets are once again fully pricing in a 25bp hike, with 26.1bps priced in for that decision (+3.1bps on the day). Then looking further out, 70bps of hikes are now priced in by the September 2027 meeting, up +6.6bps relative to Friday
